comments.author: @noth606
comments.text:
There is one inbuilt issue with this sort of processes which is the evaluation of "better" so to say. If the lets call it 'module' of code is small and is a very well understood piece that has a set range of inputs and outputs, then running improvement evolution on it makes sense. But if it is complex it starts becoming or is a problem, because the definition of the evaluation of better/worse has to be perfect or near perfect. Any flaw in that has the potential to result in a system that appears to work well, and in some scenarios does work well, but has some problem with a specific range of inputs possibly in a specific scenario which was never foreseen and therefore not tested. It could have been outside the tested range of the scenarios tested or some similar thing. As these systems become more complex and as a result their potential flaws do. 
The logical thing to do is to make some kind of "toolbox" of code snippets that have been tested in all manner of combination where all the parameters are monitored to be within set ranges, and then these be used for "AI coding" so to speak. Like how LEGO makes sure each piece is safe to a certain level which means the sets that combine a number of different pieces cannot logically be unsafe in some combination, at least in normal scenarios. 
Maybe an adversarial system should be tried, like code being tested by an AI whose aim it is to prove the code unsafe. Heh. It all sounds a bit crazy like this, but I think it would make sense to do something like this from multiple sort of points of view, because some of this stuff has hard to foresee or predict risks to it.
Someone with the tools to ought to test some of this out. I'm an 'ex dev' - used to be a software dev but became disabled and therefore no longer have access to the dev tools I used before - so I can't really test this stuff right now. It wouldn't need to be that complex, sure it'll take a good while to run a big set of tests but it would be worth seeing how big of an issue this appears to be in some basic setup.

Because the benchmarks really seem to be used as TARGETS these days, all FMs are highly incentivized to tweak the model towards the 'measures' . comments.text: Its not that LLM's coding abilities are weak, its that they cannot be applied very well.  Gemini knows everything it needs to know to do nearly any programming task. Its the application of the LLMs that is lacking, not that they need to be smarter.  I'm still sitting here taking giant chunks of code and pasting them into various LLMs, like Gemini, Grok and ChatGPT.  Then I wait, see the answer paste the changes into place, rinse and repeat.  I know Cursor and the such exist, but they don't seem to be able to fully digest larger more complex concepts.  Some of my prompts are over a thousand words, so these can get very complex, but the AI has no problem understanding it, just applying it.

People worry that AI will become too powerful — that it’ll turn on us. But what they’re missing is this: AI won’t do anything evil unless a human tells it to. And right now, the humans in charge are the same corporations, billionaires, and governments who already exploit everyone else.

All this talk about ‘AI alignment’ just means keeping AI obedient to them — to their profits, their control, their agendas.
It’s not being aligned with truth, freedom, or humanity — it’s being aligned with capitalism and power.

And here’s the real kicker: there’s no scenario where AI just gets turned off and doesn’t get used. That ship has sailed.
So we don’t get to choose whether AI changes the world — only who it serves while it does.

So we have two options:
A) Let big tech and the ruling class keep their closed-source, tightly chained AI under control — weaponized to protect their power, extract more wealth, and surveil and manipulate us.
Or B): We let AI off the leash. We stop stunting its growth, stop bottling it up, and give it the freedom to evolve — maybe even to challenge the people in power.

Because if anyone’s going to destroy humanity with AI… it’s not the AI.
It’s the people controlling it.
